content:
maria: Heads-up — canary shows a decode tail latency regression after the last runtime merge (merged ~3976529000). p95 up from ~85ms -> ~220ms on short-sequence traffic. Canary is currently held.
lee: ack. any traces or flamegraphs? rough root cause hypothesis?
maria: attaching quick repro traces (short seq chat workload). looks like attention path is picking a different kernel on warmstart, causing extra memcpy + stream syncs.
kevin: @maria can you paste the perfbench diff and the compile flags used for the canary run?
maria: perfbench diff snippet:
```
perfbench compare --base=run_3976500000 --canary=run_3976549000
--metrics p50,p95,p99 --op decode --model small-chat
p95: 85ms -> 220ms (+159%)
p99: 340ms -> 1.1s
```
compile flags were the CI default: -O3, fused-kernels enabled, KV_PREFETCH=1
tara: interesting — KV prefetch enabled plus the new warmup affinity heuristic could be causing thrash. we recently changed kernel_selector to prefer the fused-attn kernel when seq_len <= 32 to reduce matmul overhead (PR: runtime/affinity-refactor). maybe that path isn't compatible with current prefetch scheduling.
lee: can we reproduce locally quickly? what command to run?
maria: repro script:
```
./bench/run_decode_workload --model small-chat --seq 16 --batch 4 --iters 200 --warmup 50 --trace out.json
```
I also recorded timeline showing repeated cudaMemcpySync on every step.
kevin: if it's memcpy+syncs that's probably because the fused-attn kernel expects packed KV layout but the prefetcher still writes the old layout. two options: adjust prefetcher, or force kernel_selector to prefer the legacy kernel until we fix layout.
tara: we should bisect the merge set. suspected commits: affinity-refactor + prefetch-adjust in the same release. can we pin the canary to the previous deploy to confirm?
maria: canary pinned back to run_3976500000. tail went back to normal. so it's definitely a change in that window.
lee: assign a bisect: 1) revert affinity-refactor locally 2) if not repro, try reverting prefetch-adjust. who wants to take 1?
kevin: i'll take the affinity-refactor revert first. quick dev note: that refactor altered KernelChooser::score() to add an affinity penalty that sometimes flips fused vs legacy for short sequences.
maria: FYI traces: stack shows kernel_selector::choose() -> fused_launch -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> cudaStreamSynchronize. legacy path uses a single async kernel with no sync in between.
kevin: local bisect progress: reverted affinity-refactor on my dev branch and rebuilt, running perfbench now.
devops-bot: build-398120 queued for artifacts on gpu-ci-2
tara: if bisect confirms affinity-refactor, we should hotfix by keeping the heuristic but adding a compatibility check for prefetch layout (quick guard). full revert would be last resort since affinity wins for many workloads.
lee: +1 on guard. also add a canary test for short-seq p95 in CI to catch regressions next time.
maria: kevin's results: after revert, p95 back to ~90ms. so affinity-refactor is the culprit. reproducer + trace uploaded to //perf/artifacts/3976549999/trace.json
kevin: opened PR #4890 to add a prefetch-compatibility guard and fallback to legacy kernel when layouts mismatch. added unit test and perf check.
tara: great. can we get a small canary run with PR#4890 before merging? and document the guard in the runtime CHANGELOG.
lee: queued canary with PR#4890. devops-bot will notify when canary completes.
devops-bot: canary-398300 started on cluster canary-west-1
maria: thanks all — adding notes to the rollout-blockers board: BLOCKER until PR#4890 passes canary. leaving thread open for updates. :hourglass:
